results.prompt: a 3-input AND gate: three levers, and a lamp that lights only when all three are on
results.finalLine: DONE: `design.rsd.json` is a 3-input AND gate for Java (three levers, each inverted by a torch, joined on one dust line and inverted again to drive the lamp); it passed all 8 truth-table tests on the first validate round, with no diagnostics.

results.prompt: a hidden 2x2 piston door with a button on each side
results.finalLine: DONE: `design.rsd.json` passed `rsd validate` on the first round with no errors or warnings, and all 5 tests pass in the simulator. Two torches hold the four sticky pistons out to close the 2x2 wall; a floor button on either side turns them off, so the door opens for the button pulse and closes again.

results.finalLine: GAVE UP: I wrote a NOR gate to `design.rsd.json` (both levers attach to one stone block, a torch on that block lights the lamp, with 4 truth-table tests), but it has not been validated because permission to run Bash, and so `rsd validate`, was denied.

results.prompt: an XNOR gate: a lamp that is lit when two levers are in the same position
results.finalLine: - **Both on:** a second torch that only lights when both levers are on.

results.prompt: a lamp that toggles on and off each time a button is pressed
results.finalLine: DONE: the design validated on the first round with no diagnostics, and all 3 tests pass in the simulator. It is a master-slave T flip-flop built from two repeater latches. The lamp stays off with no press, turns on after one press, and is still on 80 ticks later. Because each test starts fresh from the design as written, the tests can't press the button twice, so the press that turns the lamp back off is untested and should be checked in game.

results.prompt: a clock that blinks a lamp while a lever is on and stops when it is off
results.finalLine: DONE: `design.rsd.json` passed `rsd validate` on the first round with no diagnostics. Turning the lever on lets a torch-and-repeater clock blink the lamp; turning it off holds the clock block powered so the lamp stays dark. All 6 timed tests pass in the simulator, but it hasn't been checked in game.

results.prompt: a lever that lights a lamp 40 blocks away
results.finalLine: DONE: `design.rsd.json` passed validation on the first round with no diagnostics, and both tests pass (lever off leaves the lamp off, lever on lights it within 10 ticks) — a lever at x=0 feeds a dust line with east-facing repeaters at x=16 and x=32 to a lamp at x=40, all on a stone floor, with `meta.edition` set to "java".

results.prompt: a pulse extender: a button press keeps a lamp lit for at least 3 seconds
results.finalLine: DONE: `design.rsd.json` passes `rsd validate` with no diagnostics after 2 rounds, and its 6 tests show the lamp lit at ticks 4, 15, 25 and 31 after a press (3.1 s) and off at tick 60. The button pulse runs through a chain of 8-tick repeater stages, and each stage feeds the lamp's wire through a one-way repeater; in round 1 the lamp never lit, so I extended that wire and moved the lamp (and its output position) one block east, without changing any tests.

results.prompt: a 1-bit memory cell: a set button turns a lamp on, a reset button turns it off, and it stays that way
results.finalLine: DONE: `design.rsd.json` is a Java Edition latch built from two cross-wired redstone torches. The set button turns the lamp on, the reset button turns it off, and it holds that state. It passed validation on the second round with no diagnostics. The four tests check that the lamp starts off, comes on after Set, is still on 40 ticks after Set, and is off after Reset. The first round failed only because the circuit settled with the lamp on, so I wrote the starting torch and dust states into the design so it starts off. The simulator is approximate, so it hasn't been checked in the game itself.

results.prompt: a lamp that lights only when exactly one of two levers is on
results.finalLine: DONE — `design.rsd.json` (Java Edition) uses two subtract-mode comparators, each giving "this lever and not the other", feeding the lamp; it passed `rsd validate` on the first round with no diagnostics, and all four truth-table tests pass in the simulator but it hasn't been built in game.
